permitName: Mount Rainier National Park Wilderness and Climbing Permits

description.cancellation_policy:
Cancellation Policy: You may cancel your reservation four or more full days before your reservation date and receive a refund. The $6 reservation fee is non-refundable. 

Change Policy: You may make changes to your permit itinerary, if space is available, up until the day before your reservation date (additional fees may apply). Your start date cannot be changed without cancelling your permit and starting over. Once your permit has been issued, you cannot make changes to the permit unless approved by a ranger at a Wilderness Information Center.

One additional permit holder can be identified when the reservation is created. Otherwise, reservations and permits are non-transferrable.
description.comment_box_description: Please provide additional trip details, such as: climbing route, organized group affiliation, activity (skiing, trail running, etc.), stock use on authorized trails, or general comments about your trip.
description.description:
Ascending to 14,410 feet above sea level, Mount Rainier stands as an icon in the Washington landscape. An active volcano, Mount Rainier is the most glaciated peak in the contiguous U.S.A., spawning five major rivers. Subalpine wildflower meadows ring the icy volcano while ancient forest cloaks Mount Rainier’s lower slopes. Wildlife abounds in the park’s ecosystems.

In 1988, Congress designated 97% of Mount Rainier National Park as wilderness. This area is managed to preserve its wilderness character. Tens of thousands of visitors encounter the wilderness on overnight trips every year, whether through the challenge of a summit climb, the immersion of the Wonderland Trail, or the restorative peace of a shorter foray into the backcountry.

Only a few hours away from major population centers, the Mount Rainier Wilderness provides outstanding opportunities for solitude in a landscape largely unmodified by modern human manipulation and control.
description.driving_directions:
Longmire Wilderness Information Center:

Drive east on Hwy 706 from Ashford for 10 miles. The Wilderness Information Center is located in the Longmire Historic District, 6.5 miles past the Nisqually Entrance to Mount Rainier National Park.

White River Wilderness Information Center: 70002 State Route 410, Enumclaw 98022. (Closed in Winter)

Follow WA-410 to approximately mile post 62.5. Turn onto the White River/Sunrise Rd. The WIC is located just past the White River Entrance Station.

Carbon River Ranger Station: Located at 35415 Fairfax Forest Reserve Rd E, Carbonado, WA 98323. (Currently no public access from SR 165: WSDOT News Release 4/14/25 )

Follow WA-165 past Wilkeson and Carbonado to the intersection with the Fairfax Forest Reserve Road. Turn left and follow the Fairfax Road east for 4 miles. (Currently no public access from SR 165: WSDOT News Release 4/14/25) )
description.fee_policy:
Lottery Application/Permit Reservation Fee: Each early access lottery application or permit reservation is subject to a non-refundable $6.00 fee. If you are successful in the early access lottery, no additional permit reservation fee is due. 

  • Note: The park also charges the $6 permit reservation fee for first-come, first-served permits issued in person. This fee supports the permit and reservation management system.

Recreation Fee: $12 per person, per night (starting with the February 2025 lottery). Youth 15 and under are free 

  • Note: In January 2025, the park restructured wilderness recreation fees to directly fund staff and services that support backcountry use. 

Entrance Fee: The park charges an entrance fee which you may pay upon arrival or purchase in advance. The park honors valid America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. Visit the park's Fees & Passes page for details.
description.lottery_information:
Because demand for wilderness camps and high-use climbing routes exceeds capacity during peak periods, an optional early access lottery is available. This lottery limits the number of users competing simultaneously for multi-night itineraries, which allows for more complete itineraries overall.

Successful applicants are granted early access to reservations, with the earliest access offering the most options to build a complete Wonderland Trail circuit or secure permits for the most desirable dates.

Lottery participants with later access might not have access to their preferred itinerary but can create an alternate trip using available camps.

Successful applicants will be provided a date and time that their individual access window opens. Applicants may create a reservation at any time after their access window opens. Participants are limited to a single reservation during the early access period, but may create additional reservations beginning April 25. Learn more here.
description.need_to_know_email:
This reservation is not your wilderness camping or climbing permit.

  • You must pick-up your wilderness permit in person. Permits may be picked up the day your trip starts, or one day before, at one of the park offices listed below.

  • Check winter road status before leaving home.

  • Your reservation will be held until noon of the day your hike or climb begins. After noon, your reservation will be cancelled, unless you indicate "late pickup" in the comment field of your permit, or call one of the Ranger Stations listed below to arrange a late pickup.

  • This reservation is valid only for the dates and specific camp locations that are indicated on the permit.

  • Violation of the terms and conditions of your permit may result in cancellation of your permit, termination of your trip, and a citation. 

  • Note: Your camping or climbing itinerary may be modified by the park without prior notice due to unforeseen events or emergencies.

Climbers: Each member of your party must pay the annual climbing fee. Fees must be paid online at pay.gov Solo climbs are not permitted without prior approval. Apply here . 

Cancellation Policy: Cancel your reservation 4 or more full days before your reservation date for a refund. 

Change Policy: Make changes to your permit itinerary up until the day before your reservation date. Your start date cannot be changed without cancelling your permit and starting over. Once your permit has been issued, you cannot make changes to the permit unless approved by a ranger.

Reservation fees are non-refundable.

description.need_to_know_order:
This reservation is not your wilderness camping or climbing permit.

  • You must pick-up your wilderness permit in person prior to starting your hike or climb.
  • Your reservation will be held until noon on the day your hike or climb begins. After noon, your reservation will be cancelled, unless you indicate "late pickup" in the comment field of your reservation or talk to a ranger at 360-569-6650 to arrange a late pickup. A late pickup will be held until 5:00pm.
  • Travel above 10,000 feet or on glaciers also requires a climbing special use permit (obtained at the park) and payment of the annual climbing fee (pay.gov). Solo climbs require prior approval. Apply here. 
  • Reservations are non-transferrable.
  • Groups with 24 or more people are required to apply for a Special Use Permit. 

Regulations:

  • All food, garbage, and scented items must be hung from a bear-pole or secured in an approved canister. Animal resistant food canisters are required for all Paradise area winter camping.
  • Bear Canisters are strongly recommended in cross-country and alpine areas
  • Camping is only permitted for the camp area and dates designated on your permit itinerary.
  • The maximum party size is 5 for standard sites. The maximum party size is 12 for designated group sites, Alpine zones, and Winter zones. There is no maximum group size for Paradise winter large group camps.
  • Stock are prohibited in most camp areas and trails.
  • Pets, weapons other than firearms, vehicles, bicycles and other wheeled devices are not permitted on park trails or in any undeveloped area of the park. 
  • The use of firearms is prohibited in the national park. 
  • Violation of the terms and conditions of your permit may result in cancellation of your permit and/or a citation.
description.need_to_know_permit:
When planning your trip, please keep the following in mind:

  • Permits are required year round. For information about winter camping, please start here 
  • Recreation.gov provides access to view availability and to secure reservations for permits. Pre-planning using the Wilderness Trip Planner , the Mount Rainier National Park website, and other trip planning resources such as guide books is strongly encouraged.
  • Travel above 10,000 feet or on glaciers requires a climbing special use permit and payment of the annual climbing fee. Climbing permits can be obtained in person at a Wilderness Information Center. A wilderness permit is still required, and reservations are encouraged for peak season.
  • Solo travel above high camps or anywhere on glaciers is not permitted except with prior written permission of the Superintendent. Submit a request for a solo permit. 
  • Visitors interested in a complete Wonderland Trail itinerary or other high-demand camps during peak season are encouraged to participate in the Early-Access reservation lottery. 
  • Because camping off itinerary can affect camping opportunities for others and damage natural resources, your itinerary must be achievable. For this reason, the maximum daily mileage between camps is limited to 17.5 trail miles on Recreation.gov. Trips with longer daily mileage can be obtained in person or reserved in advance by contacting the Wilderness Information Centers after the early access period ends.
  • It is possible to book reservations for areas that present life-threatening hazards and require specialized equipment and experience.
  • Non-stop itineraries that span two calendar days, such as ultra-running or single-push summit climbs, still require a permit for safety and visitor use management purposes. 
  • In designated camps, all food, garbage, and scented items must be hung from a bear-pole or secured in an approved animal-resistant canister. Permit holders may borrow bear canisters for free at Wilderness Information Centers.
  • Bear Canisters are strongly recommended in cross-country and alpine areas where it is not possible to hang food 12 feet high and 10 feet out from a tree trunk.
  • Camping is only permitted in the camp area designated on your permit itinerary, on the date indicated.
  • Excluding Paradise winter group camps, the maximum party size is 5-12 depending on camp area, and affiliated groups must camp and travel at least one mile apart. 
  • Stock are prohibited in most camp areas and trails. They are permitted on the Pacific Crest Trail and the Laughingwater Creek Trail. 
  • Pets, weapons other than firearms, vehicles, bicycles and other wheeled devices are not permitted on park trails, meadows, or in any undeveloped area of the park. 
  • The use of firearms is prohibited in the national park. 
  • Parties of 6 or more must camp in designated group sites. Parties of 5 or less must not camp in group sites unless specifically indicated on their permit.
  • A park Entrance Fee is required for entry into the National Park. Pay your entry fee in person or online. 

Leave No Trace 

Please follow all principles of Leave No Trace including: Plan ahead and prepare, travel and camp on durable surfaces, dispose of waste properly, leave what you find, minimize campfire impacts, respect wildlife, and be considerate of other visitors. 

For more information on planning your trip in the wilderness of Mount Rainier National Park, visit our Wilderness Trip Planner.
description.no_show_policy: No Show Policy: If you do not cancel and decide not to use your reservation, none of the fees will be refunded. Please cancel your reservation if you are unable to use it as this makes space available for others.
description.quota_details:
Overnight wilderness use is restricted to designated camps and zones. The number of parties that may stay overnight in the wilderness is limited by the number of campsites and by established zone use limits.

When searching availability and creating your permit, we reccommend viewing by "Daily Groups." This will display how many sites are available in each camp. 

Some alpine zones (the main climbing routes) are limited by total number of individuals. We reccommend viewing availability for these sites by "People."

The maximum party size is 5 people and 3 tents for standard trailside camps. Parties of 6-12 must camp in designated group camps while backpacking, or on snow while climbing in Alpine Zones.
description.season_information:
A permit is required year-round for all overnight stays in the backcountry. A wilderness permit allows the permit holder and their group to camp in a designated camp or area.

2/3 of wilderness permits are available for advance reservation for trips between the end of May (May 1 for climbing camps and zones) and the first federal holiday in October. Reservations must be made at least 2 days in advance of the trip start. The remaining 1/3 of permits are issued at ranger stations on a first-come, first-served basis. Sites/zones become available for reservations on April 25. See below for information on the Early Access Lottery.

Wilderness and Climbing permits outside of the reservation season are first-come, first-serve.

Off-season climbing permits are issued by self-registration at the Paradise Old Station.

Permits for the Paradise large group winter camps (13 or more people) can be reserved when consolidated snow depth at Paradise reaches 5 feet.

Visit Plan Your Visit for more information.
